FLASHSCORE PREVIEW

After Lille’s hopes of challenging for the Ligue 1 title were dashed in the last round, visiting a Le Mans side riding high on the back of a stirring comeback may be inopportunely timed.

Match News and Current Form

Le Mans produced the shock result of last weekend’s action as they overturned a 2-0 deficit away to Marseille to win 3-2, just the second time they’ve ever recovered from two goals down to win a Ligue 1 game. The bigger prize was bringing an end to their five-match winless run (D2, L3) and opening up a three-point cushion to the bottom two, as survival remains their primary goal in what is their first Ligue 1 campaign in 16 years. Tightening up at the back may hold the key to boosting their chances, as Le Mans have conceded in each of their last six home league outings, just one shy of their longest such run in the 21st century.

Lille slipped off the pace in the Ligue 1 title race after going down 1-0 at home to Lyon in the last round, but they responded in midweek with a stirring 2-1 win against European giants Bayern Munich. The Mastiffs would be forgiven for expecting a repeat result here too, as they’ve won six of their last eight Ligue 1 matches immediately following a European game (D2), while hitting the road should only further fuel belief. Lille have picked up eight more points on the road (29) than at home (21) in Ligue 1 in 2026, and having won all three away league matches this term against sides sitting ninth or lower pre-round, confidence should be high of adding to that tally here.

Head-to-Head History

Lille won each of the last three H2Hs and haven’t lost away to Le Mans since January 1999 (W2, D6).

Opta by StatsPerform
Hot Stats and Streaks

Le Mans haven’t conceded a home league goal in the opening 30 minutes this season.

Three of Le Mans' last four Ligue 1 goals have been scored by substitutes.

Lille have lost just one of their last 23 Ligue 1 matches against promoted sides (W18, D4).

Lille had fewer shots than their opponents in four of their five away league matches this term.

Key Players to Watch and Missing Players

Louis Mafouta sparked Le Mans’ comeback against Marseille, with that the only victory he’s collected in his last nine scoring appearances for club or country (D2, L6). Lille’s Hákon Haraldsson could get them off to a flying start having seen six of his last eight goals open the scoring.

Le Mans look to have no fresh injury concerns, while Lille’s Tanguy Nianzou missed their midweek European outing. 

For all the latest team news, please check the Flashscore match centre.

Betting Analysis

With Lille strong on the road and after European matches, an away win seems to be the logical choice here.

Author: Chris Wilson
